methods.description: Verify all 72 issue-declared whole-file input pins against the current checkout and exact baseline Git blobs before work; validate the 279-ID unique subject list and its pinned roster hash; run the hash-pinned retained audit twice while intercepting only its three known writes to exclusive destinations under the owned path; compare all three byte outputs against original pinned outputs.

conclusions.text: The two retained national variants each contain 3,233 unique shapeIDs; all exact 279 scoped Atlas IDs join once by shapeID in both. The reproduction matches all three original #981 outputs byte for byte.

The retained catalog digest identifies the exact simplified GeoJSON object; it is distinct from the full GeoJSON digest. The 2018 boundary vintage, 2023 source-data update, 2023 build and 2026 retrieval timestamps remain separately identified.

This is source/ID lineage only; legal and current boundaries, national or regional completeness, universal county equivalence, precise geographic accuracy, and legal reuse applicability of source/product terms remain unresolved.

The metadata identifies Census MAF/TIGER but does not identify the exact underlying Census product file or establish that Cartographic Boundary File caveats directly describe this GeoBoundaries dataset.

notes: All source input pins map exactly to issue #1154 input_1 through input_72 at c42f4b7465964245ecbcd8eed4961eb76af3106b; total baseline input bytes 237038540.
The 279 subject parent counts are cross-referenced to the already reviewed #428 Census crosswalk; GeoBoundaries shapeGroup=USA does not supply per-feature state parent evidence.

The source notice requires attribution per its terms; this packet reports its language but does not adjudicate legal applicability. ZIP and TopoJSON payloads remain unrestored; only pinned LFS pointers were checked.
